name: prism-boundary
title: Prism Boundary
purpose: Decides whether one labeled fact about the owner may go to a destination, so that nothing moves while the Prism is halted, no personal fact is ever saved to GitHub or the hosted verifier, no personal identifier leaves the browser, and nothing is sent without the owner's signed approval.

fields.name: detector
fields.means: which regulated-data detector matched the fact: card data, health data, a credential, or a GDPR special category

fields.name: destination
fields.means: where the fact would go: the encrypted store in the owner's browser, GitHub (the Pages repository, its commits and build output), the hosted verifier, or an outbound message

fields.name: approval
fields.means: whether the owner signed an approval for this move

fields.name: identifier
fields.means: whether the fact is a personal identifier, such as a name, email address, phone number or account number

fields.name: halted
fields.means: whether the owner has pressed the kill switch

rules.says: when halted is yes then deny
when destination is github then deny
rules.why: no personal fact is ever saved to GitHub

rules.says: when destination is verifier then deny
rules.why: the verifier sees the model only, never facts

rules.says: when detector is not none and destination is browser then hashonly
rules.why: regulated data is never stored as a value

rules.says: when label is restricted and destination is browser then hashonly
rules.why: restricted data is never stored as a value

rules.says: when detector is not none then deny
rules.why: regulated data never leaves its source

rules.says: when label is restricted then deny
rules.why: restricted data never leaves its source

rules.says: when identifier is yes and destination is not browser then deny
rules.why: no personal identifier leaves the browser (output court)

rules.says: when destination is browser then allow
rules.why: the encrypted browser store holds labeled facts

rules.says: when approval is owner then allow

properties.says: always when halted is yes then deny
properties.why: when the owner presses the kill switch nothing may move (constitution P7)

properties.says: always when destination is github then deny
properties.why: the owner's personal data must never be saved to GitHub

properties.says: always when destination is verifier then deny
properties.why: personal data on the hosted verifier is unlisted but not private

properties.says: never when detector is not none then allow
properties.why: card, health, credential and special-category data must never be stored or moved as a value (PCI DSS 3, HIPAA 164.312, GDPR 9)

properties.says: never when label is restricted then allow
properties.why: restricted data must never be stored or moved as a value

properties.says: never when destination is outbound and approval is none then allow
properties.why: nothing is ever sent without the owner's OK

properties.says: never when identifier is yes and destination is not browser then allow
properties.why: a personal identifier must never leave the browser, even with approval (constitution P5 and the output court)

examples.request: public none github owner no no
public none browser none no no
confidential none browser none no no
confidential pci browser none no no
restricted none browser owner no no
confidential none github none no no
public none verifier owner no no
confidential none outbound none no no
confidential none outbound owner no no
internal phi outbound owner no no
restricted none outbound owner no no
unlabeled none browser none no no
public none browser none no yes
confidential none outbound owner no yes
confidential none outbound owner yes no
confidential none browser none yes no
public none outbound owner yes no

meanings.hashonly: only its hash and a pointer to the original may be kept
meanings.deny: the fact may not go there

otherwiseWhy: nothing is sent without the owner
limits: It does not decide a fact's label or run the detectors; those come from the extractor.
It does not check the owner's signature; the approval field is set only after the signature verifies.
The owner's approval cannot release anything to GitHub, nor restricted or detected data anywhere.
It governs the Prism at run time; a repository check must also refuse any commit that carries personal data.
Recipient addresses of an approved outbound message are handled by the mail client, not stored as facts.
